documentInventory.covers: Full PRD: product overview, goals, personas, functional requirements, UX, narrative, success metrics, technical considerations, milestones, user stories
Technical specification: solution structure, project layout, command tree, output contract, data storage, keychain integration, auth providers, trace system, test strategy
Project vision and design exploration: CliqApiMcp replacement rationale, cross-platform constraints, agent-first design, preliminary architecture ideas
Decision: .NET 10 / C# 13 as runtime and language
Decision: OS-native keychain via P/Invoke with AES-256-GCM encrypted-file fallback; no third-party NuGet keychain package
Decision: all stdout/stderr output is valid JSON; fixed symbolic error code vocabulary; three exit codes (0, 1, 2)

projectSummary.name: cliq-cli
projectSummary.description: A standalone, self-contained command-line binary providing a deterministic, scriptable interface to Zoho Cliq REST APIs. Manages multiple Zoho accounts, handles authentication via a pluggable interface (PAT in v1, OAuth2 in v2), and exposes a general-purpose HTTP API invoker.
projectSummary.problem: CliqApiMcp (the predecessor macOS MCP server app) could not run headlessly, required a running UI session for authentication, and was tied to internal Zoho CocoaPod dependencies (ZMacAuth, PEXLibrary). No cross-platform, headless-capable, agent-friendly Cliq API CLI exists.
projectSummary.replacementFor: CliqApiMcp — macOS-only Cliq API MCP server over stdio
primaryConsumers: AI agents — GitHub Copilot CLI Skills and Claude Agent Skills that invoke cliq-cli as a subprocess
Zoho developers — interactive terminal use, pipeline composition with jq
projectSummary.coreWorkflow: Agent or human invokes `cliq-cli <command-group> <command> [flags]` → cliq-cli authenticates via PAT/OAuth, validates host allowlist, dispatches HTTP request to Zoho Cliq API → structured JSON to stdout (success) or stderr (error).
keyProperties: Single self-contained binary, .NET 10 / C# 13, no runtime pre-install required
Platforms: macOS (Intel + Apple Silicon), Windows x64, Linux x64
Auth: PAT-first via IAuthProvider; OS-native keychain (P/Invoke) or AES-256-GCM file fallback
All stdout/stderr output is valid JSON; fixed symbolic error codes; exit codes 0 / 1 / 2
Compile-time HTTP host allowlist; ZohoCorp domain hard-block (unconditional, dual-layer)
Passive trace recording: all api call invocations auto-appended to active session JSONL

business: Replace CliqApiMcp with a cross-platform, headless-capable alternative distributable via GitHub Releases and standard package managers.
Enable AI agent workflows (Copilot, Claude) to drive Zoho Cliq API operations without human interaction.
Establish a versioned, stable output contract (JSON envelopes + symbolic error codes) that agent skill manifests can depend on across releases.
Provide a single tool consolidating Cliq account management, API invocation, real-time event buffering, and session tracing.
user: Developers: add, manage, and switch between multiple Zoho accounts; invoke any Cliq REST endpoint without writing boilerplate HTTP code.
AI agents: receive machine-parseable JSON from every command invocation; handle errors generically using symbolic codes without per-command parsing logic.
Zoho engineering teams: record, export, and post-mortem complete API call traces across multi-step analysis sessions.
nonGoals: Native AOT compilation (deferred post-v1; PublishSingleFile with JIT is sufficient).
Interactive TUI / shell mode — output contract is pure JSON; no styled terminal output.
Support for ZohoCorp employee accounts (*@zohocorp.*) — hard-blocked unconditionally.
OAuth2 authorization code (browser-redirect) flow — v2 OAuth uses an API-based terminal flow with no browser, no redirect URL, no local HTTP listener.
Plugin or extensibility system for third-party command groups — command tree is fixed at compile time in v1.
Automatic token rotation or expiry handling in v1 (PATs are long-lived; no refresh logic until OAuth2).
CI/CD pipeline automation, GitHub Actions release workflows, multi-RID artifact publishing, code-signing automation, and Homebrew tap publishing — deferred to a dedicated DevOps phase after v1 GA.

personas.name: Vasanth / Internal Zoho Developer
personas.description: Senior Zoho engineer exploring Cliq APIs for a new integration feature. Uses cliq-cli interactively to prototype API calls, register useful endpoints in the registry, and package calls into an agent skill.
needs: JSON output that pipes cleanly into shell tools (jq)
Multi-account management across datacenters (EU, US, IN)

personas.name: Copilot Agent (AI)
personas.description: GitHub Copilot Agent instance running a CLI Skill. Calls cliq-cli as a subprocess for each API interaction. Issues commands, parses stdout JSON, and branches on the 'code' field in stderr on failure.
needs: Machine-parseable JSON on stdout and stderr for every invocation
Fixed symbolic error code vocabulary — error-handling logic written once, works for all commands
No interactive prompts in any code path

roleBasedAccess.capabilities: Add, remove, and manage all configured accounts on the local machine. Access governed by the PAT/OAuth token's own permissions against the Zoho Cliq API.
Inherits account permissions at the token level. Cannot manage accounts directly — account configuration must be completed by a human before the agent skill is invoked.
Hard-blocked at both 'account add' and 'api call' regardless of invoker. Error code: ACCOUNT_DOMAIN_BLOCKED.

functionalRequirements.description: Add, list, remove, show, set-default, and re-auth-stub account operations.
details: account add: stores PAT in OS keychain, writes metadata (without token) to accounts.json; fetches email from Zoho user-info API to validate PAT and perform ZohoCorp domain check before persisting.
account list: returns all accounts with token values masked; valid JSON.
account remove: deletes keychain secret and accounts.json entry atomically.
account show: returns full metadata with token rendered as '***'.
account set-default: updates is_default in accounts.json; subsequent commands resolve to this account when --account is omitted.
account re-auth: stub in v1 returns clear 'not yet supported' error; fully implemented with OAuth2 in v2.

functionalRequirements.area: PAT authentication and secure credential storage
functionalRequirements.description: OS-native keychain storage via P/Invoke with AES-256-GCM encrypted-file fallback.
details: macOS: Security.framework (Keychain Services)
Windows: Credential Manager (advapi32.dll CredWrite/CredRead)
Linux: Secret Service (libsecret)
No third-party keychain NuGet dependency.
Encrypted-file fallback (AES-256-GCM, machine-derived key) activates automatically on headless/CI environments.
IAuthProvider.GetTokenAsync injects 'Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken <token>' into every outgoing request.
Token values must never appear in any output, log, or file in plain text.

functionalRequirements.description: Call any Cliq REST endpoint with configurable method, path, headers, query params, and body.
details:
api call --method --path

[--body |--body-file ] [--header k:v]... [--query k=v]...
--body and --body-file are mutually exclusive; violation produces INVALID_ARGS before any network I/O.
Paths not starting with '/api/' are automatically prefixed with '/api/v2'.
Fully resolved request host validated against compile-time allowlist before HttpClient.SendAsync.
Hosts not on allowlist produce HOST_NOT_ALLOWED, exit 1.
Returns raw API response as {"status":"ok","data":<response>} on stdout.

functionalRequirements.description: Record OAuth scope metadata per account; scaffolded for v2 enforcement.
details: scope add --scope <s>: appends scope string, sets needs_reauth = true.
scope remove --scope <s>: removes scope, sets needs_reauth = true.
scope list: returns scope array as JSON array in success envelope.
api call on account with needs_reauth = true returns NEEDS_REAUTH, exit 2.
In v1, account re-auth returns 'not yet supported'; no partial OAuth flow attempted.

functionalRequirements.description: Passive capture of all api call invocations as append-only JSONL entries within a named session.
details: trace session start --name <n>: creates active session; sessions.json entry written.
All api call invocations while a session is active append a trace entry to <session-name>/trace.jsonl without extra flags.
Authorization headers unconditionally excluded from all trace entries.
trace session export --name <n>: emits JSON array to stdout; non-destructive.
--truncate-body <bytes>: limits body field lengths in export without modifying on-disk file.
trace session close: marks session inactive; file preserved.
trace session remove: deletes session entry and all files.
If no session is active, api call proceeds normally and silently skips trace — no error emitted.
Concurrent api call invocations in the same session use file locking to serialize seq counter increments.

functionalRequirements.area: ZohoCorp block and HTTP host allowlist
functionalRequirements.description: Unconditional security controls — dual-layer ZohoCorp domain block and compile-time HTTP host allowlist.
details: Any email whose host's first DNS label equals 'zohocorp' (case-insensitive) is rejected at account add with ACCOUNT_DOMAIN_BLOCKED, exit 1. Covers all datacenter TLDs without a TLD list.
Block enforced inside PatAuthProvider.StoreTokenAsync AND ApiClient.CallAsync — cannot be bypassed at command layer.
HTTP allowlist suffixes: .zoho.com, .zoho.eu, .zoho.in, .zoho.com.au, .zohoapis.com, .zohoapis.in.
Hosts not on allowlist produce HOST_NOT_ALLOWED, exit 1; no network I/O performed.
No flag, environment variable, or config file can override either restriction.

functionalRequirements.description: All commands write only valid JSON to stdout (success) and stderr (error). No plain text in any code path.
details: Success envelope: {"status":"ok","data":<payload>}
Error envelope: {"status":"error","code":"<SYMBOLIC_CODE>","message":"<human-readable>"}
Symbolic error codes: ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND, AUTH_FAILURE, NEEDS_REAUTH, HOST_NOT_ALLOWED, ACCOUNT_DOMAIN_BLOCKED, INVALID_ARGS, REGISTRY_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND (and others as defined in tech spec).
Exit codes: 0 = success, 1 = general error, 2 = auth failure / needs-reauth.
util time-ms: current UTC time as Unix millisecond timestamp.
util uuid: generate a random UUID v4.

functionalRequirements.description: Named Pex/WMS WebSocket connections with per-account JSONL event buffering and drain.
details: pex connect [--account <n>]: opens WMS WebSocket; buffers events to <configDir>/cliq-cli/pex-buffer/<account>.jsonl.
pex drain [--account <n>]: atomically reads and truncates buffer; returns events as JSON array; appends pex trace entries with relatedApiSeq correlation.
pex clear: discards buffer without returning events.
pex listen: streams events to stdout as JSONL (blocking; Ctrl+C to stop).
pex close: closes WebSocket.
Token values never appear in Pex buffer files.

functionalRequirements.description: Local catalogue of named Cliq API endpoints with method, URL template, and purpose.
details:
api registry add --id --method --url-template --purpose

: upserts entry into registry.json.
api registry list: returns all entries as JSON array.
api registry show --id <id>: returns single entry.
api registry remove --id <id>: deletes entry; REGISTRY_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND if not exists.
registry.json format compatible with existing CliqApiMcp registry for seamless migration.

functionalRequirements.description: OAuthProvider as a drop-in IAuthProvider replacement; API-based terminal flow; no browser required.
details: OAuthProvider implements IAuthProvider; ApiClient and all command classes require no changes.
account add supports --client-id and --client-secret flags when OAuthProvider is active.
account re-auth: exchanges new token via Zoho OAuth API; sets needs_reauth = false.
OAuth tokens stored in OS keychain: cliq-cli:<accountName>:oauth.
No browser window, redirect URL, or local HTTP server required at any point.
scope add/remove triggers needs_reauth = true; api call returns NEEDS_REAUTH until re-auth is run.

functionalRequirements.description: Named WebSocket connections with connect, send, listen, and close subcommands. Streaming JSONL output for listen.

stdout.notes: No plain text, no ANSI escape sequences, no styled terminal output in any success code path.

files.description: Account metadata — name, domain, is_default, needs_reauth, scopes[]. Token values never stored here.
Append-only JSONL trace entries for each active session. Authorization headers excluded.
Pex/WMS event buffer per account (v2). Atomically read and truncated by pex drain.
API registry catalogue — named endpoints with method, URL template, purpose (v2). Compatible with CliqApiMcp format.
AES-256-GCM encrypted PAT/OAuth token file — fallback when OS keychain is unavailable.

technologyDecisions.keyConsequence: Cross-platform single binary via PublishSingleFile --self-contained; nullable reference types enforced; TreatWarningsAsErrors=true
Command tree maps naturally to cliq-cli <group> <command> [flags]; auto-generated help; strongly-typed command settings

technologyDecisions.decision: OS-native keychain via P/Invoke, no third-party NuGet
technologyDecisions.keyConsequence: Security.framework (macOS), CredWrite/CredRead (Windows), libsecret (Linux); AES-256-GCM file fallback for headless
stdout = success JSON envelope; stderr = error JSON envelope; fixed symbolic error codes; exit 0/1/2
PatAuthProvider in v1; OAuthProvider is additive in v2 with zero changes to ApiClient or command classes
First DNS label of email host == 'zohocorp' (case-insensitive) → ACCOUNT_DOMAIN_BLOCKED; enforced at StoreTokenAsync AND ApiClient.CallAsync; no override path
Allowed suffixes: .zoho.com, .zoho.eu, .zoho.in, .zoho.com.au, .zohoapis.com, .zohoapis.in; HOST_NOT_ALLOWED if no match; no network I/O before check

keyAbstractions.contract: GetTokenAsync(accountName) → bearer token injected as Authorization header

keyAbstractions.role: HTTP dispatch layer; enforces host allowlist, ZohoCorp block, and Authorization injection; wraps response in JSON envelope; calls TraceWriter if session active
Appends trace entries (request, response, timing, account) to session JSONL file; unconditionally strips Authorization headers; uses file locking for seq counter

zohoCorpBlock.rule: First DNS label of email host == 'zohocorp' (case-insensitive) → reject
zohoCorpBlock.bypass: None — no flag, env var, or config can override

tokenProtection: Tokens stored exclusively in OS keychain or AES-256-GCM encrypted file — never in accounts.json, stdout, stderr, or trace files

integrationPoints.description: Primary target API; base URL derived from account domain field; all calls subject to compile-time host allowlist
Called at account add to validate PAT and retrieve email for ZohoCorp domain check
macOS Security.framework, Windows Credential Manager (advapi32.dll), Linux Secret Service (libsecret) — all via P/Invoke without third-party NuGet packages
SKILL.md in .github/skills/cliq-cli/ describes available commands; Copilot invokes cliq-cli subprocesses and reads stdout JSON
Analogous skill manifest; same JSON output contract consumed
Real-time event stream; buffered per account to JSONL; drained and correlated with api call traces

userStories.title: Account management
userStories.description: As a Zoho developer, I want to add, list, view, and remove Zoho account credentials from the CLI so that I can manage access to multiple Zoho datacenters from a single tool without manually handling tokens.
acceptanceCriteria: account add --name <n> --token <pat> [--domain <d>] stores the PAT in the OS keychain and writes metadata (without the token) to accounts.json.
account list returns all accounts with token fields masked; output is valid JSON.
account show --name <n> returns full metadata with '"token": "***"'.
account remove --name <n> deletes the keychain secret and the accounts.json entry atomically.
account set-default --name <n> updates is_default in accounts.json; subsequent commands resolve to this account when --account is omitted.
Adding a *@zohocorp.* account returns ACCOUNT_DOMAIN_BLOCKED, exit 1, and no data is persisted.
All outputs are valid JSON envelopes on stdout (success) or stderr (error).

userStories.title: PAT-based authentication and secure credential storage
userStories.description: As a Zoho developer, I want PAT credentials stored securely in the OS-native keychain (or an encrypted file fallback on headless systems) so that tokens are never exposed in plain text in any file, log, or output.
acceptanceCriteria: On macOS, Windows, and Linux, IKeychainProvider uses the platform-native store without any third-party NuGet keychain package.
On headless environments, EncryptedFileKeychainProvider activates automatically using AES-256-GCM with a machine-derived key.
Token values do not appear in stdout, stderr, accounts.json, or any trace file under any circumstances.
Unit tests for PatAuthProvider and ApiClient use an in-memory IKeychainProvider mock — no real OS keychain interaction required.
IAuthProvider.GetTokenAsync injects 'Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken <token>' into every outgoing request.

userStories.title: REST API invocation
userStories.description: As a Zoho developer and as a Copilot AI agent, I want to call any Zoho Cliq REST endpoint with full control over method, path, headers, query parameters, and body.
acceptanceCriteria: api call dispatches the request and returns the response as {"status":"ok","data":<response>} on stdout.
--body and --body-file are mutually exclusive; using both produces INVALID_ARGS on stderr before any network I/O.
Paths not starting with '/api/' are automatically prefixed with '/api/v2'.
The fully resolved request host is validated against the compile-time allowlist before HttpClient.SendAsync; hosts not on the list produce HOST_NOT_ALLOWED, exit 1.
AI agents receive parseable JSON on both stdout and stderr for every invocation.

userStories.title: Scope management
userStories.description: As a Zoho developer, I want to record OAuth scope metadata per account so that when OAuth2 is activated in v2, cliq-cli can enforce re-authentication after scope changes without a breaking schema migration.
acceptanceCriteria: scope add --scope <s> appends the scope string and sets needs_reauth = true.
scope remove --scope <s> removes the scope and sets needs_reauth = true.
scope list returns the scope array as a JSON array in the success envelope.
api call on an account with needs_reauth = true returns NEEDS_REAUTH, exit 2.
In v1, account re-auth returns a clear 'not yet supported' error; no partial OAuth flow is attempted.

userStories.title: Session trace recording and export
userStories.description: As a Zoho developer and as a Copilot AI agent running an analysis session, I want API calls to be automatically recorded to a named persistent trace so that I can export and review the complete call history after the session ends.
acceptanceCriteria: trace session start --name <n> creates a new active session; sessions.json entry added with status: active.
All api call invocations while a session is active append a trace entry to <session-name>/trace.jsonl without any extra flag on api call.
Authorization headers are absent from all trace entries.
trace session export --name <n> emits a JSON array of all entries to stdout without modifying the .jsonl file.
--truncate-body <bytes> limits body field lengths in the export without modifying the on-disk file.
trace session close marks the session inactive; trace session remove deletes session entry and all files.
If no session is active, api call proceeds normally and silently drops the trace entry — no error emitted.

userStories.title: Security controls — ZohoCorp block and HTTP host allowlist
userStories.description: As the cliq-cli security owner, I want all ZohoCorp-domain accounts unconditionally blocked and all outgoing HTTP requests restricted to known Zoho datacenter hosts.
acceptanceCriteria: Any email whose host's first DNS label equals 'zohocorp' (case-insensitive) is rejected at account add with ACCOUNT_DOMAIN_BLOCKED, exit 1.
The block is also enforced inside PatAuthProvider.StoreTokenAsync and ApiClient.CallAsync — cannot be bypassed by future command additions.
Any outgoing request URL whose host does not match a suffix in the compile-time allowlist is rejected with HOST_NOT_ALLOWED, exit 1 — no network I/O is performed.
No flag, environment variable, or config file can override either restriction.
Unit tests verify both blocks using in-memory fakes — no real network or keychain access.

userStories.title: Cross-platform self-contained binary distribution
userStories.description: As a Zoho developer, I want to download a single self-contained binary for my platform and use cliq-cli immediately without installing .NET or any other runtime.
acceptanceCriteria: dotnet publish -r <rid> /p:PublishSingleFile=true --self-contained true produces a working binary for win-x64, osx-x64, osx-arm64, and linux-x64.
The binary runs on a clean OS (no .NET SDK installed) and produces valid JSON on the first invocation.
Binary size per RID ≤ 80 MB.
TreatWarningsAsErrors=true and <Nullable>enable</Nullable> enforced in all .csproj files; build fails on any warning or nullable violation.

userStories.title: Pex / WMS real-time event buffering
userStories.description: As a Copilot AI agent running a Cliq API analysis session, I want to connect to Cliq's Pex/WMS real-time event stream, buffer events locally, and drain them as a JSON array.
acceptanceCriteria: pex connect opens a Pex/WMS WebSocket and begins buffering events to <configDir>/cliq-cli/pex-buffer/<account>.jsonl.
pex drain atomically reads and truncates the buffer; returns all events as a JSON array and appends pex trace entries with relatedApiSeq correlation.
pex clear discards buffered events without returning them.
pex listen streams events to stdout as JSONL (blocking; Ctrl+C to stop).
pex close closes the WebSocket.
Token values never appear in Pex buffer files.

userStories.title: OAuth2 authentication
userStories.description: As a Zoho developer, I want to authenticate accounts using OAuth2 (machine-to-machine, no browser) with fine-grained scope enforcement.
acceptanceCriteria: OAuthProvider implements IAuthProvider; ApiClient and all command classes require no changes.
account add supports --client-id and --client-secret flags when OAuthProvider is active.
account re-auth --name <n> exchanges a new token via the Zoho OAuth API and updates the OS keychain; sets needs_reauth = false.
OAuth tokens stored in keychain as cliq-cli:<accountName>:oauth.
scope add/remove triggers needs_reauth = true; api call returns NEEDS_REAUTH until re-auth is run.
No browser window, redirect URL, or local HTTP server is required at any point.

userStories.title: API registry
userStories.description: As a Zoho developer, I want to maintain a local catalogue of named Cliq API endpoints with methods, URL templates, and purpose descriptions.
acceptanceCriteria:
api registry add --id --method --url-template --purpose

upserts an entry into registry.json.
api registry list returns all entries as a JSON array.
api registry show --id <id> returns a single entry by ID.
api registry remove --id <id> deletes the entry; REGISTRY_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND when ID does not exist.
registry.json format is compatible with the existing CliqApiMcp registry format.
All operations return valid JSON envelopes.

technicalChallenges.challenge: P/Invoke correctness across three OS keychain APIs
technicalChallenges.mitigation: Dedicated integration tests on macOS, Windows, and Linux for each platform keychain implementation

technicalChallenges.challenge: Self-contained binary size (50–80 MB per RID)
technicalChallenges.mitigation: Native AOT is the long-term mitigation (post-v1); PublishSingleFile with JIT is acceptable for v1

technicalChallenges.challenge: New Zoho datacenter TLDs not in compile-time host allowlist
technicalChallenges.mitigation: API calls will fail until a new binary is released; ZohoCorp domain check is TLD-agnostic by design but the allowlist is not — monitor Zoho infrastructure announcements

technicalChallenges.challenge: OAuth2 scope enforcement — advisory only in v1
technicalChallenges.mitigation: Full enforcement requires OAuth2 (v2); v1 scope metadata is advisory only; PAT with broad permissions can call any endpoint regardless of recorded scopes
Distribution via notarized binary or Homebrew tap required for smooth installation; deferred to post-GA DevOps phase
